The candidate state is appropriate: lastRain stores the previous fill time for each lake, while an ordered set stores past dry days that have not yet been assigned. A repeated rain creates a deadline whose required dry day must be strictly after that lake previous rain.

Using dryDays.higher(prev) selects the earliest feasible unused dry day. Since the set contains only already-observed days, the selected day is automatically before the current rain; choosing the earliest feasible day preserves later dry days for future windows with later left boundaries.
If higher(prev) does not exist at the repeated-rain deadline, no unused past dry day lies inside the required interval, so that flood is unavoidable and returning an empty array is correct.
